items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: Marcus Belgrave who kind of was like helped oh like Kenny Garrett, Geri Allen, Robert Hurst, a lot of people played with him

ctx.x: Sheila Jordan told me a pretty horrific story about the racial atmosphere in Detroit that would have been — she’s somewhat older of course, but did you witness anything like that going to those clubs with your father?

Yes, only in the sense of like I often would be the only white person within a few miles, not only of the club but like in the entire neighborhood. And I remember the first time I went, there was a famous trumpet player Marcus Belgrave who kind of was like helped oh like Kenny Garrett, Geri Allen, Robert Hurst, a lot of people played with him and he kind of like continued that lineage of like Donald Byrd and Yusef Lateef and Charles McPherson and all those amazing, you know Elvin and all those Detroit — Joe ©…

Henderson, Pepper Adams — all the people who came through Detroit — Hank Jones. I mean I could go on, the list is so vast. So Marcus was like the guy when I was growing up. So I went and I had met Robert Hurst, Bob Hurst, the bass player and so he said, “Well you can come and sit in.” So I was there waiting my turn to sit in you know, I didn’t want to just like run up to the stage you know. So at the end of the set it was like the vibe was a little bit like I hadn’t met them and it was like you know, but it…
